scope.flow: Distributor._setClaimRecipient stores claimRecipient[user][token] = recipient but emits ClaimRecipientUpdated with arguments in an order that swaps the token and recipient topics relative to the declared event signature
scope.environment: on-chain Merkl Distributor contract; off-chain indexers, analytics pipelines and payout automation consuming the emitted event

statements.text: _setClaimRecipient stores claimRecipient[user][token] = recipient, establishing an on-chain mapping from a user and token to a recipient.
The ClaimRecipientUpdated event is declared with parameter order (user, token, recipient).
The emit site passes ClaimRecipientUpdated(user, recipient, token), swapping the token and recipient arguments relative to the declaration.
The event declaration order (user, token, recipient) does not match the emitted argument order (user, recipient, token).
In the emitted log the indexed token topic actually holds the recipient address and the recipient topic holds the token address.
Off-chain indexers that rebuild claimRecipient from the event construct the inverse mapping and pair tokens with the wrong recipients.

For each _setClaimRecipient call the emitted ClaimRecipientUpdated log should carry the token in the declared token position and the recipient in the declared recipient position, so off-chain reconstruction of claimRecipient[user][token] matches on-chain state.
Off-chain reporting, accounting and payout automation rely on the event topics to determine recipients rather than reading on-chain storage.

ambiguities: No attacker, authorization or permissionless-call condition is described; the scenario involves a contract-internal event-emission mismatch.
No concrete submitted transaction, user or token values are provided, so the described state is a possible scenario rather than an observed incident.
Whether any actual off-chain payout was misrouted is reported as potential (will/can), not as an asserted loss.
